title: 細胞の構造と機能
subtitle: Structure and Function of the Cell
keywords: Cell structure 2.Cell function 3.Signal transduction 4.Gene expression 5.Experimental techniques
educationalGoal: Cells are important elements of all living things on Earth. Humans, plants and animals, every living organism, is composed of cells. Naturally, if cells are the structural and functional units of living things, there must be something peculiar about them. What is it about cell structure and function that make them so important?
advice: This course will cultivate understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern cells, the structural and functional units of living things. The basic cellular processes of organelles and localization, movement, proliferation and signal transduction in cells will be introduced. To cultivate your familiarity of the science behind what we know from modern biology, we will discuss the experimental techniques utilized to study cell structure and function. The lectures are designed to be interactive. In addition to instructor presentations, we will often break into short discussions about current issues and analyze data. Additionally, students will give feedback in questionnaires given in the classroom on the successes and failures of each lecture in order to continually improve the course. This course will work on your skills in scientific writing. We will discuss how to read and interpret primary contents of the textbook, and how to construct precise and concise scientific writing.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology.

activityGoals.body: Describe the basic cellular signaling process
Describe the application of cell biology in industry

achievementLevels.ideal: Describe the following concepts and discuss the progress of the field of modern biology: (1) the molecular mechanisms that govern basic cellular functions such as cell proliferation and signal transduction. (2) the science behind what we know from modern biology. (3) the experimental techniques utilized to study cell biology in several model systems including yeast, frogs, fish, mice, and mammalian cells in culture.
